activity_context.topic_title: The Sum of a Finite Geometric Series

feedback.problem: If $k(1+{(\frac{1}{7})}^{13})$ is the sum of the first $13$ terms of the geometric series $49-7+1-⋯,$ then $k=$
feedback.worked_solution:
Given a geometric series, the sum of the first $N$ terms is given by the formula

$$
{S}_{N}={a}_{1}\frac{(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r},
$$

where ${a}_{1}$ is the first term of the series and $r$ is the common ratio.

In our case, ${a}_{1}=49.$ To find the value of $r,$ we find the ratio of the first two terms in the series:

$$
r=\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}}=\frac{-7}{49}=-\frac{1}{7}
$$

If we substitute ${a}_{1}=49,N=13$ and $r=-\frac{1}{7}$ into our formula, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{13} & =49\cdot \frac{(1-{(-\frac{1}{7})}^{13})}{(1-(-\frac{1}{7}))} \\  & =49\cdot \frac{(1+{(\frac{1}{7})}^{13})}{(1+\frac{1}{7})} \\  & =49\cdot \frac{(1+{(\frac{1}{7})}^{13})}{(\frac{8}{7})} \\  & =\frac{49}{(\frac{8}{7})}\cdot (1+{(\frac{1}{7})}^{13}) \\  & =\frac{343}{8}\cdot (1+{(\frac{1}{7})}^{13})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, comparing the expression above with $k(1+{(\frac{1}{7})}^{13}),$ we obtain $k=\frac{343}{8}.$
